behaviours.title: A deposit credits the account and records a deposit entry
behaviours.given: a new Ledger with no accounts
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('alice') is 100 and entries('alice') is one entry { txnId: 't1', kind: 'deposit', amount: 100 }
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is refused with reason 'unknown-account' because 'alice' was never opened, and her balance stays 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted but balance shows 10000 (cents) instead of 100
the deposit is accepted but no history entry is recorded

behaviours.title: A deposit of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('alice') stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero deposit is accepted as a no-op and reported as { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the zero deposit is accepted and a deposit entry of 0 is recorded

behaviours.title: A negative deposit is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the negative deposit is accepted and the balance becomes 50
contrary_alternatives: the negative amount is treated as 50 and accepted, so the balance becomes 150

behaviours.title: Repeating a deposit with the same txnId has no further effect
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 100 was deposited to 'alice' with txnId 't1'
behaviours.when: 100 is deposited to 'alice' again with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance stays 100 and there is still only 1 entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the second deposit is applied too and the balance becomes 200
contrary_alternatives: the second deposit is rejected with reason 'duplicate' and the balance stays 100

behaviours.title: A txnId used by a deposit makes a later withdrawal with the same txnId a silent no-op
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 100 was deposited to 'alice' with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } but nothing is withdrawn: the balance stays 100 and there is 1 entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is applied (txnIds are tracked per operation type) and the balance becomes 49.5
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected with reason 'duplicate' and the balance stays 100

behaviours.title: Deposit amounts are rounded to the nearest cent, with 1.005 rounding up to 1.01
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the balance is 1.01
behaviours.contrary_then: the balance is 1 (the half cent is dropped)
contrary_alternatives: the balance is stored unrounded as 1.005
the deposit is rejected because it has more than 2 decimal places

behaviours.title: A deposit of exactly half a cent over (0.125) rounds half up to 0.13
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the balance is 0.13
behaviours.contrary_then: the balance is 0.12 (rounding half to even / down)
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected for having sub-cent precision

behaviours.title: A deposit of 0.001 is accepted but credits nothing and records an entry of 0
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance is 0 and one deposit entry with amount 0 is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is refused with reason 'amount-too-small' and no entry is recorded
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted and the balance becomes 0.01 (rounded up)
the deposit is accepted and the balance holds 0.001 unrounded

behaviours.title: An account that was never used reads as balance 0 with no entries
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: balance is 0 and entries is an empty list
behaviours.contrary_then: balance returns undefined for an unknown account
contrary_alternatives: reading an unknown account throws an error (the read is refused)

behaviours.title: Opening an existing account does not reset it
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 50
behaviours.then: the balance stays 50 and the deposit entry is kept
behaviours.contrary_then: the account is re-created and the balance becomes 0
contrary_alternatives: open is refused with an error because the account already exists

behaviours.title: The list returned by entries is a copy; changing it does not change the history
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 50 was deposited to 'alice'
behaviours.when: the list returned by entries('alice') is emptied and entries('alice') is read again
behaviours.then: the second read still returns 1 entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the history is emptied too and the second read returns 0 entries
contrary_alternatives: the returned list is read-only and emptying it is refused with an error

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit is converted at the given rate
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance is 150 and a 'deposit' entry of 150 is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: the balance is 100 (the rate is ignored)
contrary_alternatives: the balance is 66.67 (amount divided by the rate)
the deposit is refused because 'alice' was never opened

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit with rate 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected with reason 'amount-too-small' instead
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted and credits 0

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit with amount 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is accepted as a no-op with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected with reason 'amount-too-small'

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit worth less than half a cent is rejected as amount-too-small and does not use up its txnId
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.when: depositForeign('alice', 1, 0.004, 'f1') is made (worth 0.004), then 5 is deposited with txnId 'f1'
behaviours.then: the foreign deposit returns { ok: false, reason: 'amount-too-small' } with no entry, and the later deposit of 5 is applied so the balance is 5
behaviours.contrary_then: the foreign deposit is accepted crediting 0, and the later deposit with the same txnId is ignored so the balance stays 0
contrary_alternatives: the foreign deposit is rounded up, accepted and credits 0.01

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit worth exactly half a cent rounds up to 0.01
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance is 0.01
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected with reason 'amount-too-small' and the balance stays 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted but credits 0

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit reusing a txnId is a silent no-op
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 100 was deposited to 'alice' with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the foreign deposit is applied and the balance becomes 120
contrary_alternatives: the foreign deposit is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: A small withdrawal is charged the minimum fee of 0.50, included in the withdrawal entry
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 20
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance is 9.5 and the withdrawal entry has amount 10.5 (10 plus 0.50 fee)
behaviours.contrary_then: the fee is 1% (0.10) and the balance becomes 9.9
contrary_alternatives: no fee is charged and the balance becomes 10
the fee is charged but the entry shows only 10
the withdrawal is refused because the fee makes it too small to be worthwhile

behaviours.title: A withdrawal of 100 is charged a 1% fee of 1.00
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 1000
behaviours.then: the balance is 899
behaviours.contrary_then: the minimum fee of 0.50 applies and the balance is 899.5
contrary_alternatives: no fee is charged and the balance is 900
a 2% fee is charged and the balance is 898
the withdrawal is refused and the balance stays 1000

behaviours.title: The withdrawal fee is rounded up to the next cent
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 1000
behaviours.then: the fee is 1.01 and the balance is 898.98
behaviours.contrary_then: the fee is rounded down to 1.00 and the balance is 898.99
contrary_alternatives: the fee is rounded to the nearest cent (1.00) giving 898.99
the withdrawal is refused and the balance stays 1000

behaviours.title: The withdrawal fee is capped at 25.00
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 5000
behaviours.then: the fee is 25 and the balance is 1975
behaviours.contrary_then: the uncapped fee of 30 is charged and the balance is 1970
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected for exceeding a single-withdrawal limit and the balance stays 5000

behaviours.title: A withdrawal that uses the whole balance including the fee is allowed
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 101
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with 'insufficient-funds' and the balance stays 101
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is allowed only if the balance stays above 0, so it is refused

behaviours.title: A withdrawal the balance covers but not with the fee is rejected
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 100.99
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and the balance stays 100.99
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal goes through and the balance becomes -0.01
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal goes through with the fee reduced to fit, leaving balance 0
the withdrawal goes through without a fee leaving 0.99

behaviours.title: Withdrawing exactly the daily limit of 5000 is allowed (the fee does not count toward the limit)
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 6000 and has withdrawn nothing
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance is 975 (5000 plus the 25 fee)
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with 'daily-limit' because 5000 plus the fee exceeds 5000
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected because the limit is exclusive (must be under 5000)

behaviours.title: A single withdrawal of 5000.01 exceeds the daily limit
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 6000
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and the balance stays 6000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal goes through (accepted with { ok: true })
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is capped at 5000 and goes through

behaviours.title: The daily limit is cumulative across withdrawals and is never reset within a Ledger
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 10000 and has already withdrawn 3000 (balance 6975)
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and the balance stays 6975
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal goes through because each withdrawal is checked on its own
contrary_alternatives: the fee counts towards the limit so even 1975 more would be refused

behaviours.title: After withdrawing 3000, a further 2000 exactly reaches the limit and is allowed
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 10000 and has already withdrawn 3000 (balance 6975)
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance is 4955
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with 'daily-limit' and the balance stays 6975
contrary_alternatives: the earlier fee of 25 counts toward the limit, so the withdrawal is refused

behaviours.title: Each account has its own daily withdrawal limit
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' and 'bob' each have 6000 and 'alice' has already withdrawn 5000
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and bob's balance is 975
behaviours.contrary_then: bob's withdrawal is rejected with 'daily-limit' because the limit is shared across the ledger
contrary_alternatives: bob's withdrawal is refused and his balance stays 6000

behaviours.title: Insufficient funds is reported ahead of the daily limit
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' }
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal goes through and the balance goes negative

behaviours.title: A rejected withdrawal does not use up its txnId or the daily limit
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 6000
behaviours.when: 5000.01 is withdrawn with txnId 'w1' (rejected), then 5000 is withdrawn with the same txnId 'w1'
behaviours.then: the second attempt returns { ok: true } and the balance is 975
behaviours.contrary_then: the second attempt is treated as a duplicate of 'w1' and the balance stays 6000
contrary_alternatives: the second attempt is rejected with 'daily-limit' because the failed attempt counted

behaviours.title: A withdrawal of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has a balance of 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted and only the minimum fee is charged, leaving 99.5
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted as a no-op

behaviours.title: A transfer moves the amount with no fee and records both sides
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 100
behaviours.when: 40 is transferred from 'alice' to 'bob' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, alice has 60, bob has 40, alice's last entry is transfer-out 40 and bob's entry is transfer-in 40
behaviours.contrary_then: a withdrawal-style fee of 0.50 is charged and alice has 59.5
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is refused because 'bob' was never opened

behaviours.title: Transferring the entire balance is allowed
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, alice has 0 and bob has 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is rejected with 'insufficient-funds'
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is refused because an account may not be emptied

behaviours.title: Transferring one cent more than the balance is rejected
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }, alice still has 100 and bob has 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer goes through and alice has -0.01
contrary_alternatives: the transfer goes through for the 100 available only

behaviours.title: A negative transfer is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and alice still has 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is accepted with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the transfer goes the other way and is accepted: bob sends 5 to alice

behaviours.title: Repeating a transfer with the same txnId has no further effect
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' had 100 and already transferred 40 to 'bob' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, alice stays at 60 and bob at 40
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is applied again: alice has 20 and bob has 80
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: A split of 0.05 among 3 recipients gives the leftover cents to the first recipients in order
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 1
behaviours.then: b gets 0.02, c gets 0.02, d gets 0.01 and alice has 0.95
behaviours.contrary_then: the leftover goes to the last recipients: b 0.01, c 0.02, d 0.02
contrary_alternatives: everyone gets 0.01 and the 0.02 remainder stays with alice
the remainder all goes to the first recipient: b 0.03, c 0.01, d 0.01
the split is refused because 0.05 does not divide evenly by 3

behaviours.title: A split of 100 among 3 gives 33.34, 33.33, 33.33 and debits exactly 100
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 100
behaviours.when: 100 is split from 'alice' to ['b', 'c', 'd'] with txnId 's1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }; b has 33.34, c 33.33, d 33.33, alice 0; alice's entry is split-out 100 and b's is split-in 33.34
behaviours.contrary_then: each recipient gets 33.33 and 0.01 stays with alice
contrary_alternatives: each gets 33.33 and the extra cent goes to the last recipient d
the split is refused because 100 does not divide evenly by 3

behaviours.title: A split with no recipients is rejected as no-recipients
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'no-recipients' } and alice still has 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the split is accepted and alice loses 10 to nobody (balance 90)
contrary_alternatives: the split is accepted as a no-op

behaviours.title: A split with amount 0 and no recipients reports invalid-amount first
behaviours.given: a new Ledger
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'no-recipients' }
contrary_alternatives: the split is accepted as a no-op

behaviours.title: A split with no recipients is rejected even when its txnId was already used
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 100 was deposited to 'alice' with txnId 't1'
behaviours.when: 10 is split from 'alice' to [] with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'no-recipients' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the result is { ok: true } because t1 was already processed
contrary_alternatives: the split is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: Repeating a split with the same txnId has no further effect
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' had 100 and already split 10 to ['b', 'c'] with txnId 's1'
behaviours.when: the same split is made again with txnId 's1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, alice stays at 90 and b at 5
behaviours.contrary_then: the split is applied again: alice has 80 and b has 10
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: A split larger than the balance is rejected
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 10
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }, alice keeps 10 and b has 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the split goes through and alice has -0.01
contrary_alternatives: only the available 10 is split and goes through, 5 each

behaviours.title: A full year of 5% interest on 1000 credits 50 (simple interest)
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 1000
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance is 1050 and an 'interest' entry of 50 is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: interest compounds daily and the balance is 1051.27
contrary_alternatives: the rate is treated as a fraction (5 = 500%) and the balance is 6000
interest is refused and the balance stays 1000

behaviours.title: Interest uses a 365-day year
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 365
behaviours.then: the interest is exactly 1.00 and the balance is 366
behaviours.contrary_then: a 360-day year is used, interest is 1.01 and the balance is 366.01
contrary_alternatives: a 366-day year is used and interest is 0.99
interest is refused and the balance stays 365

behaviours.title: Interest is rounded down to the cent
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 1000
behaviours.then: the interest is 4.10 and the balance is 1004.1
behaviours.contrary_then: interest is rounded to the nearest cent giving 4.11 and a balance of 1004.11
contrary_alternatives: interest is rounded up giving 4.11
interest is refused and the balance stays 1000

behaviours.title: Interest that rounds to 0 reports success, records nothing and does not use up the txnId
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 1
behaviours.when: applyInterest('alice', 1, 1, 'i1') (worth 0.0000274), then 5 is deposited with txnId 'i1'
behaviours.then: the interest call returns { ok: true } with no interest entry, and the later deposit is applied so the balance is 6
behaviours.contrary_then: the txnId 'i1' is consumed by the interest call, so the later deposit is ignored and the balance stays 1
contrary_alternatives: the interest call is rejected with reason 'amount-too-small'
interest is rounded up to 0.01

behaviours.title: Interest with rate 0 or 0 days is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' has 1000
behaviours.then: both return { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 1000
behaviours.contrary_then: both are accepted as no-ops returning { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: 0 days is accepted and treated as 1 day, crediting interest

behaviours.title: Applying interest twice with the same txnId credits it once
behaviours.given: a Ledger where 'alice' had 1000 and 5% for 365 days was applied with txnId 'i1' (balance 1050)
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance stays 1050
behaviours.contrary_then: interest is applied again on 1050 and the balance becomes 1102.5
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with reason 'duplicate'
